commits.message:
fix(artifact): add Textual's notice to THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES (rich-artifact-c9k.1)

Most of the bundled themes, and the formulas buildPalette uses to derive
a full palette from base colours, come from Textual. Textual is MIT-
licensed under its own copyright (2021 Will McGugan), which the first
commit left out. Found in code review.

fix(artifact): ship the MIT license and upstream notices (rich-artifact-c9k.1)

package.json declared MIT, but the tarball carried no license text, so
the package claimed terms it never distributed. MIT also requires every
copy to keep the upstream copyright notices, and this package draws on
two sources.

LICENSE holds the unmodified MIT text with this project's copyright.
THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES reproduces two upstream notices: Rich (Will McGugan),
the project this is a port of, and cli-spinners (Sindre Sorhus), the
source of every built-in spinner. Rich carries the cli-spinners notice
too.

They are two files so that license checkers that compare LICENSE to the
MIT template still see a close match. Appending more license text to it
would break that comparison. npm always packs LICENSE but not a notices
file, so "files" now names THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES. Two comments that
quoted files: ["dist"] now describe what that line meant: all of dist/
ships.

Verified: npm pack lists both files, and the extracted tarball contains
all three copyright lines.

test(seam): gate workflow consistency instead of keeping it by hand (rich-workflows-0pr.sut) (#130)

* test(seam): gate workflow consistency instead of keeping it by hand (rich-workflows-0pr.sut)

rich-workflows-0pr.2 put every action on one major and every job that runs
src/ on node-version-file, and nothing held either in place: .github/ was
the one area with no seam gate.

test/seam/workflow-pins.test.ts reads every YAML file under .github/ and
fails when a remote action is pinned to more than one major, and when a
bare node-version: literal appears without a row in NODE_VERSION_LITERALS,
or a row outlives its literal. code-review.yml is not exempt; its SHA pin's
"# vN" trailer is what gets read.

Regex over lines rather than a YAML parser: none is in the tree, and any
non-comment line mentioning either key in a shape the gate does not
recognise is reported as unreadable, so a new shape fails instead of
passing unseen. Dependabot was considered and not added; the header says why.

Blind spot: this checks that the files agree with each other, not that the
major they agree on is right or that any workflow runs, and it trusts a SHA
pin's trailer without checking it.

* docs(claude): describe the workflow consistency gate (rich-workflows-0pr.sut)

The section every other test/seam gate has: what it asserts, why .github/
needed one, that code-review.yml is read rather than exempt, the temptation
it guards against, and its blind spot. The gate's module header owns the
argument; the section restates neither the pinned majors nor the granted
literal.

* fix(seam): let each occurrence of a literal carry its own grant (rich-workflows-0pr.sut)

The grant table's uniqueness check forbade the second grant the count rule
requires, so a second job needing the same literal could satisfy neither.
The count rule already reports a surplus grant, so the uniqueness check
enforced nothing it did not, and is deleted.

Also split lines on CRLF as well as LF, so a Windows checkout does not read
every pin as unreadable.

* fix(seam): report a quoted workflow key as unreadable (rich-workflows-0pr.sut)

The net under the recognised forms required the colon directly after the
key name, so "uses": and 'node-version': — valid YAML, run fine by
Actions — produced no fact and no report, and a disagreeing pin or an
ungranted literal written that way passed the gate. The net now allows a
closing quote before the colon, which is what the header and CLAUDE.md
already promised: a shape the gate does not read fails loudly.
